items.title: AX is just the orchestration layer
items.excerpt: Reframes 'AX' (agent/AI experience) not as a new surface to decorate but as an orchestration layer designers must own — coordinating models, agents, and handoffs rather than hand-crafting each screen. A fresh Design-AX angle distinct from the 07-13 taste/handoff essays.

items.title: The terminal became my canvas
items.excerpt: A designer's account of craft migrating off the visual canvas and into the terminal/CLI, where prompts and code (Claude Code-style agentic tooling) become the primary design surface. A concrete vibe-coding workflow shift rather than a taste essay.

items.title: When design becomes the organisation, and AI becomes the design
items.excerpt: Argues that as AI absorbs execution, the design function reshapes into org-level structure — the 'design' increasingly is the operating system of the team rather than the artifacts it ships. A design-org transformation lens on AX.

items.title: How a tiny Star Trek film team is rethinking VFX with AI
items.excerpt: An indie Star Trek fan-film crew explains how generative AI could clear VFX's biggest bottleneck — green-screen keying and rotoscoping — pointing to where AI actually fits into a real production pipeline rather than replacing artists.

items.title: Top logo designer quits because "AI is better than me"
items.excerpt: Gary Simon (DesignCourse) reacts to a prominent logo designer publicly quitting with the line 'AI is better than me,' unpacking what the moment says about craft, identity, and where human designers still hold the edge.
